subject: humanities
passage: In 1925, Herbert Bayer, a young teacher at the Bauhaus school of design in Germany, proposed an alphabet with no capital letters at all. His reasoning was practical as much as aesthetic. German, which capitalizes every noun, required writers, typesetters, and typewriter makers to manage two complete sets of letters, and Bayer argued that a single set of simple, geometric forms would save time and effort while reading just as clearly. The Bauhaus adopted lowercase-only printing for its own publications, but the idea never spread far beyond such circles; the habit of capitals proved far more durable than Bayer had hoped.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To argue that German writers should give up the practice of capitalizing every noun
choices.B: To explain the reasoning behind a design proposal and note its limited influence
choices.C: To show how the Bauhaus persuaded printers across Germany to stop using capital letters
choices.D: To describe the geometric shapes that Bayer chose for each letter of his alphabet

explanation.why: Most of the text explains Bayer's proposal and the practical reasons behind it, such as the burden of "two complete sets of letters." The last sentence notes that the idea "never spread far beyond" the Bauhaus. The text explains the reasoning behind a proposal and notes its limited influence.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text reports Bayer's argument but does not itself argue for the change; it notes that the idea failed to spread.
explanation.B: Correct. The text sets out why Bayer wanted a lowercase-only alphabet and then says the idea did not spread widely.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text says the idea "never spread far beyond such circles," so the Bauhaus did not persuade printers generally.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text mentions "simple, geometric forms" only in passing and never describes the individual letters.
